items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: I remember a guy named Bob White -- he was a pianist -- tried his best to get me to stay in Dayton.

ctx.x: I got the shoes and my clarinet. Oh, yes. I got my shoes and clarinet. Yes, yes. The guy tried to keep me -- I remember a guy named Bob White -- he was a pianist -- tried his best to get me to stay in Dayton. I said, "No, I've got to get back to school. It's important. I've got to go back to school." And that's how I come to New York. Otherwise, I'd still been in Ohio probably -- had I not gone to Dayton and cut class and they notified my parents and they got on a train and came right out to Ohio after.
So, this was about 1919 that you actually moved to New York.
